newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Certificates tied to Israeli index to be offered.
newsitem.headline: Certificates tied to Israeli index to be offered.

text.p: Credit Suisse First Boston (CSFB) will be offering certificates based on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange Maof index of blue chip stocks starting on Tuesday, the bank's Israeli partner Dovrat Shrem said on Monday.
CSFB expects to sell at least $7 million during the initial offering, which closes on May 28, said Elchanan Maoz, head of Dovrat Shrem's international department.

The certificates will trade on the Zurich Stock Exchange and reflect the prices of the top 25 shares traded in the Israeli stock market that make up the Maof options index. Pricing will be based on the certificates' underlying net asset value.
They will be redeemed once a year when the underlying stocks are reconfigured to reflect changes the stock exchange has made in the index, Maoz said.

He said the certificates aimed to meet the growing interest of foreign investors in the Israeli stock market and to attract new investors by eliminating currency conversions and other obstacles to investing directly in the Israeli bourse.
"I think these new instruments are good for investors that want to invest in Israel but don't have the organisation or tools to chase after every company," added a spokesman for Dovrat Shrem.

The certificates, the first of their kind to be issued based on an Israeli index, will be priced in dollars. Credit Suisse will charge about two percent on buying the certificates and there will be no exit or management fee.
